c.tagline: Saxon Transylvania's medieval jewel, where the rooftops watch you back.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed taxis are metered and cheap; ride-hailing (Uber, Bolt) is widely available and often easier than flagging a cab.

emergency.note: 112 is the single EU emergency number connecting to police, ambulance, and fire.

hood_desc: The historic heart on the ridge, wrapping the Grand Square (Piata Mare), Small Square (Piata Mica) and the Council Tower; home to the Brukenthal National Museum, the Bridge of Lies and the famous eyelid-shaped 'eyes of Sibiu' rooftop windows. The walkable base for first-timers.

The atmospheric older quarter below the ramparts, a maze of pastel artisan houses, cobbled lanes and stepped passages along the Cibin; quieter and more residential, linked to the Upper Town by staircases and the Bridge of Lies.

The commercial center just south of the old core around Unirii Square, with the Radu Stanca National Theatre, shops and strong bus links; a convenient, less touristy base a short walk from the squares.
A leafy residential district beside the long Sub Arini Park and the Dumbrava forest, near the ASTRA open-air village museum and Sibiu Zoo; best for green space, jogging and a calm stay.

A traditional, budget-friendly neighborhood near the train and bus stations with local guesthouses and easy transport connections; suits travelers wanting value and quick onward links to the rest of Transylvania.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though many locals prefer bottled for taste.

transit.hours: Tursib buses run roughly 5:00 AM to 11:00 PM; there is no dedicated night service, so taxis or ride apps cover late hours.
transit.note: Sibiu has no metro or tram; the city relies on the Tursib bus network, supplemented by taxis and ride-hailing (Uber, Bolt). The compact old town is best explored on foot.
transit.pay: Buy paper tickets from Tursib kiosks or pay contactless on board; a single ride is about 3.5 lei. Validate on boarding.

bus: Intercity coaches and minibuses to Brasov, Cluj-Napoca, Bucharest and beyond
train: CFR national rail from Sibiu station to Brasov, Cluj-Napoca and Bucharest

transit.m: Tursib bus lines 11/112/116/117/118 to the center (~10-15 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving about 10% at restaurants for good service is customary.

landmarks: Piața Mare (Large Square)
Sibiu's grand baroque main square, ringed by pastel merchant houses whose eyelid-shaped attic windows seem to watch passers-by.
Bridge of Lies (Podul Minciunilor)
Romania's oldest cast-iron bridge, an 1859 landmark wrapped in legends that it creaks or collapses whenever someone tells a lie upon it.
Council Tower (Turnul Sfatului)
A 13th-century tower between the two main squares whose climbable levels open onto classic red-rooftop views of the old town.
Brukenthal National Museum
Romania's oldest museum, housed in Baron Brukenthal's baroque palace, with an exceptional collection of European old masters including Van Eyck.
Lutheran Cathedral of Saint Mary
A soaring 14th-century Gothic cathedral whose 73-metre steeple dominates Sibiu's skyline, sheltering a massive organ and medieval frescoes.
ASTRA Museum of Traditional Folk Civilisation
Europe's largest open-air museum, a lakeside forest park in Dumbrava filled with hundreds of relocated windmills, farmsteads and wooden churches.
Piața Mică (Small Square)
A charming arcaded square of craft shops and café terraces linked to the lower town by the Bridge of Lies and medieval passageways.
Passage of Stairs (Pasajul Scărilor)
A picturesque 13th-century stairway of arches and buttresses tumbling from the fortified upper town into the artisan lower town.
Holy Trinity Orthodox Cathedral
A monumental 1906 cathedral modelled on Istanbul's Hagia Sophia, its gilded Byzantine interior glowing with mosaics and frescoes.
Fortification Towers on Strada Cetății
The best-preserved stretch of Sibiu's medieval walls, where the Carpenters', Potters' and Harquebusiers' towers line a leafy promenade.

train.note: Sibiu has no reliable year-round direct international train; travellers heading abroad normally change at Brașov or Cluj-Napoca onto the Budapest and Vienna services, or join the Vienna-Bucharest 'Dacia' at Sighișoara. The station is on Piața 1 Decembrie 1918, a 10-15 minute walk from the Piața Mare, and CFR Călători InterRegio trains run to Brașov (about 3 hr 30 min), Bucharest (roughly 5 hr 30 min to 6 hr), Cluj-Napoca, Alba Iulia, Timișoara and Arad. The lines out of Sibiu are single-track and slow, so the coach is often faster to Bucharest and Cluj. Tickets are cheapest booked online a few days ahead on cfrcalatori.ro, and international tickets are sold separately at bileteinternationale.cfrcalatori.ro.

intl.to: Budapest, Vienna, Munich, Milan & other Western European cities

bus.note: Long-distance coaches use the autogara immediately beside the railway station, so rail and bus connections are easy. Sibiu is the home city of Atlassib, one of Romania's biggest diaspora coach operators, which along with FlixBus and Normandia runs to Hungary, Austria, Germany and Italy; tickets are bought online or at the counters in the autogara. Domestic minibuses and coaches leave frequently for Bucharest (about 4 hr 30 min via the Olt valley), Brașov (2 hr 30 min), Cluj-Napoca (3 hr) and Sighișoara. Since Romania joined the Schengen land-border area in January 2025, the Hungarian crossing is quick, though drivers still collect passports or ID cards before the frontier.

ferry.note: Sibiu is an inland city in the Transylvanian highlands with no navigable waterway and no sea access, so there are no ferries or passenger boats.

half.name: Sighișoara
half.blurb: A fortified medieval citadel with a colorful old town and clock tower, birthplace of Vlad the Impaler.

half.name: Alba Iulia
half.blurb: A star-shaped Habsburg-era citadel where Romania's 1918 unification was declared, with a changing-of-the-guard ceremony.

full.name: Bran Castle
full.blurb: A hilltop fortress associated with the Dracula legend, built in the 14th century to guard a mountain trade route.

full.name: Transfăgărășan and Bâlea Lake
full.blurb: A high-mountain road climbing through the Făgăraș range to a glacial lake, one of Europe's most scenic drives.

full.name: Râșnov Fortress
full.blurb: A medieval peasant citadel on a rocky hilltop above the town, built as a refuge from Ottoman and Tatar raids.
